To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Mtv-7 and exogenous Mtv-1a (MMTV(SW)) induce specific deletion of T cells expressing reactive TCR V beta domains, but only Mtv-1 induces T cell proliferation; (2) Mtv-1 is transmitted multidirectionnally between lymphocyte and mammary gland; and (3) B cells and CD4+ T cells are the most efficient APC for both Mtv-1 and Mtv-7.
Mtv's can be expressed in a variety of cells and can induce T cell deletion and anergy in the periphery.

(1) B cells and CD 8+ (but no CD4+) cells from Mtv7+ mice induce peripheral deletion of Mtv-7-specific T cells in the absence of proliferation, and (2) exogenous MMTv(SW) is transmissible between B, CD8+ and CD4+ cells and ultimately to the breast.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of tolerance to self antigens.
the molecular mechanisms that control the development of the immune system.
the role of Mtv's and Mls antigens in T cell development, activation and tolerance induction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MMTV ORFs are not expressed in all lymphocyte subsets, but are expressed in a cell type-dependent manner.
the expression of endogenous and/or exogenous MMTVs can be detected in various lymphoid subsets and that these subsets are able to induce T cell deletion and proliferation in vivo.
the MMTV ORFs are presented by B cells to T cells in a manner that results in deletion of T cells that are reactive with MMTV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of MMTV in the periphery can lead to the deletion of reactive T lymphocytes.
MMTV is transmitted multidirectionnally among different cell types, and that the MMTV gene products can induce peripheral T cell deletion in vivo.
MMTV-encoded antigens can be expressed by a wide variety of cell types, and that the presentation of these antigens by different cells results in different immunological outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exogenous Mtv's can induce T cell deletion in vivo in the absence of detectable T cell activation, whereas endogenous Mtv products induce T cell deletion and proliferation.
exogenous Mtv- 1a (Mmtv-SW) can be transmitted between different lymphocyte subsets, including B cells, and that B cells can induce peripheral deletion of Mls-1b reactive CD4+ T cells.
MMTV ORFs are efficiently transmitted between different lymphocyte subsets, which can be a source of variability in the presentation and recognition of Mls determinants by T cells.
